repos/copse-dev/agent-pane/pulls?state=o.title: Detect Codex sign-in through the codex-acp adapter's bundled CLI
repos/copse-dev/agent-pane/pulls?state=o.body:
## Problem

In Settings → Coding agents, Claude and Cursor showed **Ready** but Codex (`/opt/homebrew/bin/codex-acp`) showed no badge, even though Codex works. Follows up [#3758](https://github.com/copse-dev/agent-pane/pull/3758), which deliberately keeps failed Codex probes `unknown`.

## Cause (verified on the reporting machine)

The Codex check ran `codex login status`. `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` (2.2.2) **bundles its own Codex CLI** (`@openai/codex` 0.160.1) and installs no `codex` on PATH. On this machine `command -v codex` finds nothing, so the probe failed with ENOENT and the result stayed `unknown`. The renderer correctly shows no chip for `unknown`.

The adapter exposes its bundled CLI as `codex-acp cli …` (it honours `CODEX_PATH`, otherwise resolves `@openai/codex/bin/codex.js`). `codex-acp cli login status` on this machine prints `Logged in using ChatGPT`. No credential values were read or logged.

## Fix

`src/main/services/acp/acp-auth-status.ts`:
- The Codex check still tries a standalone `codex login status` first. If that can't answer, it asks the agent's own launch command with `cli login status` appended: the saved entry's command and args, else the catalog's `codex-acp`. That is the same CLI and credential store the agent actually runs on.
- The probe closes the child's stdin, so a launcher that ignores the arguments and starts an ACP server exits at EOF rather than waiting for the 6 s timeout.
- Semantics stay conservative. Missing, failed, timed-out and unrecognised probes remain `unknown`, and credential-file presence still never implies Ready.

No renderer change: `agentChip` already maps `signed-in` → Ready, and the Settings-open and Re-scan paths already call `acp:auth-status`.

## Acceptance criteria
- A working codex-acp-only install shows **Ready** on opening Settings and after explicit Re-scan.
- Signed out → **Needs sign-in**. A missing command or a failed/unknown probe → no chip.
- A credential file alone never yields Ready.

## Validation

**Real runtime (this machine, real `detectAcpAuthStatus` bundled from source, real CLIs):**

| Case | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Working install | `codex-acp: unknown` (the reported bug) | `codex-acp: signed-in` (~1.2 s total for 3 agents) |
| `CODEX_HOME` = empty dir (signed out) | — | `signed-out` |
| `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` (missing command) | — | `unknown` |

**Unit:** `pnpm test -- acp-auth-status` → 12/12 pass. New cases cover:
- adapter fallback when `codex` is ENOENT;
- signed-out and unrecognised adapter output;
- `npx`-style saved launch args;
- a standalone answer that skips the adapter;
- the catalog launch command passed to deps.

**E2E / visual:** `tests/e2e/settings-acp-agents-list.e2e.ts` gains a case. With no `codex` on PATH and a fixture adapter answering `cli login status` with "Logged in using ChatGPT", clicking **Re-scan** turns the chip into **Ready**, with no "Copy sign-in command". The spec also isolates `HOME`, because Re-scan reads shell startup files. It saves `settings-acp-agents-list-codex-ready.png`.
- `wdio run wdio.conf.ts --spec tests/e2e/settings-acp-agents-list.e2e.ts` → 2 passing (local macOS Electron).
- Negative control: the same spec against origin/main's `acp-auth-status.ts` → the new case fails and the existing case passes.

**Gates:**
- `pnpm run check:local` passes (typecheck, type-coverage, lint, format, dead-code, oracle). The oracle reports HIGH confidence; full check was run because auth is a mandatory surface.
- `pnpm test` (full unit): 14731/14744 passed and 12 failed. None of the failures are in or import the changed files, and all are environment failures in the agent sandbox:
  - SSH control socket path too long under `$TMPDIR` (4, `OpenSshTransport`)
  - `Unsafe review directory: /var` (6, screenshot review packets)
  - bash 3.2 `exclude_head[@]: unbound variable` (1, ci.yml invariants)
  - read-only-store pnpm preparation (1, runStage0)

  Required PR CI runs the complete gate.

## Remaining gaps
- **Sign-in command:** the signed-out row's "Copy sign-in command" (and the reauth hint) is still `codex login`, which fails with "command not found" on an adapter-only install. `codex-acp cli login` would work. That copy is shared with error messages, the usage panel and container agents, so it is left for a separate change.
- The real interactive sign-in → Re-scan transition (logging out and back in to a real ChatGPT account) was not exercised. Signed-out was verified with an empty `CODEX_HOME`, and the Ready transition with the e2e fixture.
- The new screenshot baseline will come from CI's screenshot-candidate flow (Linux); the local capture was reviewed by eye.

## Summary
- An automation schedule firing while a different project is focused in the renderer left its prompt sitting in an unsent "new thread" draft: the renderer only starts a draft automation thread via `isPendingAutomation`/`startThread`, which is gated on the active project matching the schedule's project.

- `AgentDispatcher.dispatch()` and the internal `dispatchExclusively` helper now accept an explicit target `AgentHost` instead of always emitting to the renderer's, so this headless path and the normal renderer path can share the same dispatch/claim logic.

repos/copse-dev/agent-pane/pulls/3773.title: Detect Codex sign-in through the codex-acp adapter's bundled CLI
repos/copse-dev/agent-pane/pulls/3773.body:
## Problem

In Settings → Coding agents, Claude and Cursor showed **Ready** but Codex (`/opt/homebrew/bin/codex-acp`) showed no badge, even though Codex works. Follows up [#3758](https://github.com/copse-dev/agent-pane/pull/3758), which deliberately keeps failed Codex probes `unknown`.

## Cause (verified on the reporting machine)

The Codex check ran `codex login status`. `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` (2.2.2) **bundles its own Codex CLI** (`@openai/codex` 0.160.1) and installs no `codex` on PATH. On this machine `command -v codex` finds nothing, so the probe failed with ENOENT and the result stayed `unknown`. The renderer correctly shows no chip for `unknown`.

The adapter exposes its bundled CLI as `codex-acp cli …` (it honours `CODEX_PATH`, otherwise resolves `@openai/codex/bin/codex.js`). `codex-acp cli login status` on this machine prints `Logged in using ChatGPT`. No credential values were read or logged.

## Fix

`src/main/services/acp/acp-auth-status.ts`:
- The Codex check still tries a standalone `codex login status` first. If that can't answer, it asks the agent's own launch command with `cli login status` appended: the saved entry's command and args, else the catalog's `codex-acp`. That is the same CLI and credential store the agent actually runs on.
- The probe closes the child's stdin, so a launcher that ignores the arguments and starts an ACP server exits at EOF rather than waiting for the 6 s timeout.
- Semantics stay conservative. Missing, failed, timed-out and unrecognised probes remain `unknown`, and credential-file presence still never implies Ready.

No renderer change: `agentChip` already maps `signed-in` → Ready, and the Settings-open and Re-scan paths already call `acp:auth-status`.

## Acceptance criteria
- A working codex-acp-only install shows **Ready** on opening Settings and after explicit Re-scan.
- Signed out → **Needs sign-in**. A missing command or a failed/unknown probe → no chip.
- A credential file alone never yields Ready.

## Validation

**Real runtime (this machine, real `detectAcpAuthStatus` bundled from source, real CLIs):**

| Case | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Working install | `codex-acp: unknown` (the reported bug) | `codex-acp: signed-in` (~1.2 s total for 3 agents) |
| `CODEX_HOME` = empty dir (signed out) | — | `signed-out` |
| `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` (missing command) | — | `unknown` |

**Unit:** `pnpm test -- acp-auth-status` → 12/12 pass. New cases cover:
- adapter fallback when `codex` is ENOENT;
- signed-out and unrecognised adapter output;
- `npx`-style saved launch args;
- a standalone answer that skips the adapter;
- the catalog launch command passed to deps.

**E2E / visual:** `tests/e2e/settings-acp-agents-list.e2e.ts` gains a case. With no `codex` on PATH and a fixture adapter answering `cli login status` with "Logged in using ChatGPT", clicking **Re-scan** turns the chip into **Ready**, with no "Copy sign-in command". The spec also isolates `HOME`, because Re-scan reads shell startup files. It saves `settings-acp-agents-list-codex-ready.png`.
- `wdio run wdio.conf.ts --spec tests/e2e/settings-acp-agents-list.e2e.ts` → 2 passing (local macOS Electron).
- Negative control: the same spec against origin/main's `acp-auth-status.ts` → the new case fails and the existing case passes.

**Gates:**
- `pnpm run check:local` passes (typecheck, type-coverage, lint, format, dead-code, oracle). The oracle reports HIGH confidence; full check was run because auth is a mandatory surface.
- `pnpm test` (full unit): 14731/14744 passed and 12 failed. None of the failures are in or import the changed files, and all are environment failures in the agent sandbox:
  - SSH control socket path too long under `$TMPDIR` (4, `OpenSshTransport`)
  - `Unsafe review directory: /var` (6, screenshot review packets)
  - bash 3.2 `exclude_head[@]: unbound variable` (1, ci.yml invariants)
  - read-only-store pnpm preparation (1, runStage0)

  Required PR CI runs the complete gate.

## Remaining gaps
- **Sign-in command:** the signed-out row's "Copy sign-in command" (and the reauth hint) is still `codex login`, which fails with "command not found" on an adapter-only install. `codex-acp cli login` would work. That copy is shared with error messages, the usage panel and container agents, so it is left for a separate change.
- The real interactive sign-in → Re-scan transition (logging out and back in to a real ChatGPT account) was not exercised. Signed-out was verified with an empty `CODEX_HOME`, and the Ready transition with the e2e fixture.
- The new screenshot baseline will come from CI's screenshot-candidate flow (Linux); the local capture was reviewed by eye.

repos/copse-dev/agent-pane/pulls/3688.body:
## Summary
- An automation schedule firing while a different project is focused in the renderer left its prompt sitting in an unsent "new thread" draft: the renderer only starts a draft automation thread via `isPendingAutomation`/`startThread`, which is gated on the active project matching the schedule's project.
- `automation-service.ts` now drives that thread's first turn directly from main (`runHeadlessAutomationTurn`) whenever `getActiveProjectId()` doesn't match the schedule's project, dispatching through the shared `AgentDispatcher` with no renderer involvement.
- New `headless-message-assembler.ts` persists the turn's transcript straight to the thread spine, reusing the same `addMessage`/`appendToken`/`addToolCall`/… helpers the renderer's own chunk handling uses, against a throwaway in-memory store — so there's no second, hand-rolled assembly path to drift out of sync.
- `AgentDispatcher.dispatch()` and the internal `dispatchExclusively` helper now accept an explicit target `AgentHost` instead of always emitting to the renderer's, so this headless path and the normal renderer path can share the same dispatch/claim logic.

Current source: `aac571c4ed5ae488abe14924cb01bdfe2a73c393`. No conflicts remain. The PR is ready for review; outstanding native acceptance is documented below.

Enrollment now persists profile/key identifiers before native creation, resumes the same native record after interruption, and retires pending metadata after migration commits or replays. Native create uses create-only Keychain insertion and reuses an existing record without replacing its key or weakening its authentication policy. The streamed-reply visual capture waits until streaming has occurred and then requires consecutive settled frames; a delayed-submit regression verifies that it cannot finish on the previous reply. All four Copilot review threads are resolved.

Signed enrollment resumed a pending identity using an existing native record, retained the same device key/envelope, migrated all four synthetic API/SSH/VNC records and removed pending metadata. Supported signed macOS releases now automatically migrate saved API keys and remembered SSH/VNC credentials to per-profile encryption protected by the Secure Enclave. New profiles enroll the same way. Standard startup opens silently; Settings → Storage offers “Require authentication when Copse starts.” Existing vaults that already required authentication retain that policy.

Recovery-key export always requires fresh native authentication, including when startup authentication is off or the profile is already unlocked. Changing the authentication setting and restoring a recovery key also require authentication. Recovery export includes re-import verification; restoration needs both the separately saved key and a consistent encrypted profile backup.

An unlocked session survives sleep and screen lock until quit. Cancelling startup authentication leaves the profile locked with an explicit Unlock retry. There is no Lock and restart button. Changing startup policy replaces the hardware wrapping key without re-encrypting records or invalidating recovery keys.

This implements the saved-secret portion of #2652. Conversations, repositories and browser cookies are outside its scope. Unsupported platforms and development builds retain existing storage; encrypted profiles currently require the Electron desktop. Migration verifies all source credentials and commits through a ciphertext-only journal; failures preserve the original data and expose retry guidance.

Security boundaries:

- The independently signed helper authenticates its caller using the kernel audit token. Silent access requires the exact hardened, sealed release app and its signed capability marker. Other callers require explicit native approval and authentication.
- macOS packaging disables Electron RunAsNode, Node options and inspector fuses, requires the integrity-checked app archive, rejects debugger launch options, and restricts main-process entitlements. Background workers use a separately packaged Node 24 interpreter with a distinct identity. Its official release checksums are verified before packaging.
- One atomic Keychain record owns the active device key, envelope and authentication policy. Replaying an old profile manifest cannot select an older silent key; the next successful unlock repairs stale app metadata. This does not claim resistance to restoring the OS Keychain itself.
- Native code verifies the original manifest MAC before revealing or installing a recovery key. Wrong recovery keys leave device state intact. Recovery values remain in native UI.

Same-Mac missing-native-record recovery rejected invalid-format input without state changes, then accepted the privately entered correct key and retained credential ciphertext. Startup prompt was not visible in this rollback run; explicit Unlock displayed it.

Sleep/lock, reboot, helper update, physical unplug, actual commit interruption and remaining native cancellation stages are unverified. User excludes Rosetta/x64 execution.

**Active-client acceptance failure resolved:** the signed app now preserves all four encrypted synthetic records while the production client lease is held. Removing the blocker and clicking Retry migration succeeds. Remaining native stages, lifecycle/hardware scenarios and every worker path are still incomplete. Same-Mac recovery emulation passed; physical replacement-Mac recovery is unverified. No merge or release was performed.
